- When sentiment is negative and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 1–2 days above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model overestimates recovery; shift forecast downward by 3–5% for next 5 days.  
- Model often underestimates mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; add 1–2% upward bias if recent 5-day average is below 30-day average.  
- If sentiment is positive but forecast is falling, check for lag; adjust forecast up by 2–5% if sentiment > 0.10 for 3+ days.  
- Avoid forecasting below 5% of recent 18-day low unless sentiment is strongly bullish; use sentiment as trigger for floor correction.
